clue.text: In Love Island, over-the-top to climb piece of furniture?

indicators.note: one thing set in another means the climbing piece goes inside the pair that follows

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OTT is the common abbreviation for over-the-top
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A reality-TV contestant on Love Island climbs over a piece of furniture in an exaggerated display.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British dating reality show, but here the two words are separate pieces of wordplay with the climbing piece set between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low upholstered seat or footstool, often with storage inside, so it is an item of furniture.

clue.text: Resting place bedaubed with gold? No!

parts.note: surface reading: a bed smeared with gilding, which the exclamation rejects
setter's reading: the word bedaubed holds AU, the symbol for gold; take it out and what remains is the word bed written twice over

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the idea of a bed smeared with gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: BED-AU-BED without AU leaves BED BED: a bed doubled, hence DOUBLE BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A double bed is furniture for sleeping in, a place where two people rest at night.

clue.text: Unlikely slogan for feminist troublemaker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: split as ..., a boast that men are excellent, hardly a feminist's rallying cry
second meaning: a nuisance or threat

explanation.surface: A feminist troublemaker would hardly adopt this slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: ACE as an adjective means excellent, so MEN ACE reads as a slogan praising men.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a person who causes trouble or annoyance, as in Dennis the Menace.

clue.text: Discussed an Oscar, and direction, in cowboy movie location

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so the name is heard rather than read

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish writer; his surname is pronounced like an untamed animal's adjective
a compass direction

explanation.surface: Talk about an Oscar-winning director and the setting of a western.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an Oscar' points to the Oscar Wilde type rather than an award statuette.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wild West, the American frontier, is the classic setting for cowboy films (westerns).

clue.text: Plots routes with breaks — for this?

definitions.text: Plots routes with breaks — for this?

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, all three words letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone maps out routes with stops along the way, for a hurried trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a whistle-stop tour is exactly a route plotted with many short breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle-stop tour is a rapid journey with many brief stops, as on a political campaign trail.

clue.text: Birds beginning to rise up over plant

parts.note: larks are songbirds

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning over flips the order of what precedes it
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: opening letter of rise
taken as written

explanation.surface: Birds start to rise up over a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower, a delphinium relative with spurred blue blooms.

clue.text: Devoured last of cheddar after whiskey drink

indicators.note: placing one part after another sets the order in which the parts are joined

parts.note: whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
devoured means ate

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: final letter of cheddar

explanation.surface: Someone ate up the cheese, then had a whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the most basic drink; the noun stands for any beverage here.

clue.text: Formic acid dispenser in secure place in New Mexico

indicators.note: one thing in another means the first is placed inside the second word

parts.note: secure means safe
ants spray formic acid in defence

explanation.surface: Locking away a chemical sprayer somewhere secure in New Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the state capital of New Mexico, a city in that US state.

clue.text: Device adopted by old English actor

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the first word goes inside the letters that follow

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
a tool is a device
E abbreviates English

explanation.surface: A gadget used by a veteran English performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in O'TOOLE is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter O'Toole, star of Lawrence of Arabia, was a celebrated stage and screen performer.

clue.text: Tear gas? Bother!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, by example: tear gas is a chemical that inflames the eyes
second meaning: a nuisance, something that annoys

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry on getting a whiff of tear gas.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is anything causing inflammation or annoyance, so it covers both a chemical agent and a nuisance.

clue.text: Those highest in the pecking order fancy RSPB oats

definitions.text: Those highest in the pecking order

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests something elaborately reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RSPB is Britain's Royal Society for the Protection of Birds

explanation.surface: Senior birds at the top of the pecking order are partial to oats from a bird charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass are the senior officers or leaders of an organisation, the people at the top of a hierarchy.

clue.text: Den's twisting stopped by Angie at last in television show?

indicators.note: twisting round turns the word to face the other way, so it is read backwards
a gap stopped by something is plugged, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a den is a lair; the 's makes it plural

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the name before it

parts.note: final letter of Angie

explanation.surface: Den and Angie, the famous EastEnders couple, in a scene from the soap.
explanation.walkthrough: Den and Angie Watts were landlords of the Queen Vic in EastEnders, the BBC soap opera, so the names look like characters not wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is a drama broadcast in episodes, such as a soap opera, so it is a kind of television programme.

clue.text: Bloomer involving Spooner's unclothed nether regions

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: unclothed is bare and the nether regions are hell; swap their first sounds

explanation.surface: An embarrassing blunder that exposes someone's naked lower parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or underwear, but it is a flowering plant. Nether regions here means the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A harebell is a wild flower with blue bell-shaped blooms, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Instructed extremely excitable daughter to keep gold coin

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the coin goes within
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last are kept

parts.note: outer letters of excitable
a ducat was a gold coin used across Europe
D abbreviates daughter

explanation.surface: Someone told an overexcited daughter to look after a gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated means taught or schooled, the same as having been instructed.

clue.text: Photographer's assistant's car, a Ford

parts.note: auto is short for automobile
the Focus is a Ford model

explanation.surface: The car owned by a photographer's helper is a Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after assistant stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Autofocus is a camera feature that sharpens the image automatically, helping whoever takes the picture.

clue.text: This Spurs manager to bring Son into the team?

definitions.text: This Spurs manager to bring Son into the team?

parts.words: Spurs manager to bring Son into the team
parts.note: surface reading: the Tottenham Hotspur manager selecting their star South Korean striker Son Heung-min
setter's reading: a boss giving his own son a job, which is favouritism towards family

explanation.surface: A football manager at Tottenham picks Son for the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club whose forward Son Heung-min shares his name with a family relation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to relatives, especially giving them jobs, as a manager hiring a son would.

clue.text: Most verbose start from writer — editor's bemused

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of writer

indicators.note: bemused means confused, so the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An editor is baffled by a writer's long-winded opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordy means using too many words, so the wordiest is the most long-winded.

clue.text: Enjoying continued success, as Philadelphia might be

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having a winning streak
second meaning: Philadelphia is a brand of cream cheese, which might be spread inside a bread roll

explanation.surface: A city or its sports team on a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: Philadelphia looks like the US city, but it is the soft cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: On a roll is an idiom for a run of success, and literally describes cheese spread in a bun.

clue.text: Chap with neat cut, wavy style

indicators.note: wavy suggests a line that winds about, so the letters are mixed up
cutting a word shortens it, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its tail is cut

explanation.surface: A man with a tidy haircut in a wavy style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a haircut beside 'neat', but it trims the last letter of neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence or flair, a synonym for style in the sense of dash.

clue.text: New tap in loo not required

indicators.note: new suggests something remade in a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new tap in the toilet is an unnecessary extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Optional means left to choice, so something optional is not compulsory.

clue.text: Goethe is maybe admitting a belief in God

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the phrase holds the word within its letters

parts.note: runs across the end of Goethe, all of is and the start of maybe

explanation.surface: Perhaps the German writer Goethe confesses to religious faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in the existence of a god or gods, especially one creator.

clue.text: Fool Phoebe, half-cut poetess

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool

indicators.note: cut by half means only half the name survives, here its first half

parts.note: the first half of Phoebe

explanation.surface: Phoebe, a tipsy poet, is made a fool of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which is what the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the ancient Greek lyric poet of Lesbos, the most famous female poet of antiquity.

clue.text: Tip glass of beer when getting round in

indicators.note: getting something in means taking it inside, so the ring shape goes within the drink

parts.note: a pint is a standard glass of beer in a British pub
the letter O is round

explanation.surface: Knock over a pint while getting a round of drinks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting a round in' is the British pub custom of buying drinks for the group; 'in' completes the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A point is the sharp tip of something, like the point of a pencil.

clue.text: Dry tail of large slug nipped by duck

indicators.note: something nipped by another is pinched between it, so it sits inside

parts.note: the teal is a small duck

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: last letter of large
a slug is a small shot of spirits, a tot

explanation.surface: A duck snaps at the dried-out rear of a big slug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slug' looks like the garden mollusc, but here it is a swig of liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry person or event has no alcohol; teetotal means abstaining from it entirely.

clue.text: Chamber illuminated current business minister?

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
illuminated means lit
I is the symbol for electric current
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A government minister in a lit-up parliamentary chamber, discussing current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' suggests the Commons, but it is the old word for a chamber pot. The question mark flags a minister as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a politician, and a government minister is one example of such a person.

clue.text: Mawkish American husband boring Stallone?

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the first letters go inside the name

parts.note: Sly is Sylvester Stallone's nickname
US abbreviates American
H abbreviates husband

explanation.surface: An American husband finds a Stallone film dull and sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull, but it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Slushy describes over-sentimental writing or films, just as mawkish means sickly emotional.

clue.text: Veteran sold spades scratched — send back

indicators.note: a runner scratched from a race is withdrawn, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
S abbreviates spades in card games

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to remit is to send, as with money

explanation.surface: An old soldier sells his spades but has to return them.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-timer is someone with long experience, which is what a veteran is.
